Title:
Manipulation of information flow and thermodynamic performance in nonreciprocal quantum dot information engines
Authors:
Hao Feng
,
Junjie Liu
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Quantum information engines leverage information as a thermodynamic resource to facilitate energy conversion. In the operation of such engines, the information flow between the working substance and the controller is pivotal, however, strategies for its efficient manipulation remain largely unexplored. Here, we investigate an autonomous information engine based on a double-quantum-dot setup, where a downstream dot coupled to two reservoirs acts as the working substance, and an upstream dot coupled to a single reservoir serves as the controller. By extending the second law of thermodynamics to incorporate the effects of nonreciprocal couplings between the dots and their electronic reservoirs, we develop a thermodynamic framework that allows us to demonstrate that nonreciprocity can significantly modulate the inter-dot information flow, thereby providing a robust control mechanism. We show that the influence of nonreciprocity can be equivalently understood through a mapping to an effective reciprocal system upon a reparameterization of chemical potentials and the electron-electron coupling strength. We further analyze the impact of nonreciprocity on the engine's performance and operation regime. Our findings establish nonreciprocal coupling as an effective control knob for designing and optimizing quantum dot information engines, surpassing the capabilities of conventional reciprocal configurations.

Within this framework, the causal-history dynamics generate a structural constraint compatible with γ_A. Within the two-channel integer-multiplicity family, (p,q)=(1,1) is further shown to be the unique discrete architecture compatible with the previously established DUT value γ_A, establishing algebraic uniqueness within this causal class. This consistency supports the interpretation of γ_A as a robust structural parameter of causal coarse-graining rather than a model-specific artifact. We develop a unified analysis based on the non-minimally coupled scalar action, exact compactification of z = ξS², slow–fast reduction, exact second-order response theory, minimal state-space realization, and Mori–Zwanzig projection. The exact transformation O = z/(1 + z), D = 1/(1 + z) implies D/O = 1/z. The microscopic response possesses a minimal two-dimensional realization and, away from critical damping, two distinct simple physical poles. Exact temporal sampling proves that the signed local scalar amplitude does not coincide with the positive history-counting variable, while projection onto the relevant scalar–curvature observable yields the explicit memory kernel K(t) = PLQ · e^(QLQt) · QLP; for the locally stationary damped realization this reduces to K(t) = −ω² · e^(−Γt), with effective projected resolvent G_eff(s) = (s + Γ)/(s² + Γs + ω²). The causal-history architecture is represented by two exhaustive, disjoint unit-cardinality extension classes, giving p = q = 1 and hence N_n = N_(n−1) + N_(n−2). The resulting ratio map R_(n+1) = 1/(1 + R_n) has the unique positive stable fixed point R_* = (√5 − 1)/2. Identifying the asymptotic ordered fraction with this scale-invariant ratio yields D/O = O and maps exactly to z_c = (1 + √5)/2. The resulting prediction γ_A = 0.618034 is fixed before observational comparison and is directly testable with Euclid, DESI, and CSST growth data.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202609.2210.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 9, 24]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7197564\", \"title\": [\"Decoherence, Epistemic Coarse-Graining, and the Emergence of Classical Causal Structure\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>This paper demonstrates that classical causal structures necessarily emerge from the quantum formalism under the resource constraints of finite agents. The Kochen-Specker and Bell theorems falsify the existence of a global Kolmogorov joint probability and Reichenbach's Common Cause Principle at the pure quantum level, leaving Pearl's do-calculus undefined in the undecohered algebra A SE.
